Pendulum_obs and resonator_lab have each undergone genuine small physical shifts (instrument or environment), independent of one another; pendulum_lab and resonator_obs remain stable because they are better thermally or electromagnetically isolated.
Weak multi-day oscillatory or damped-resonance artifact in measurement apparatus or building environment is beginning to manifest; post-baseline drifts are early signs of quasi-periodic modulation.
Measurement or data-logging error: post-baseline readings contain systematic bias (calibration drift, offset, or transcription mistake) not present in baseline.
Residual: something not yet articulated (e.g., systematic artifact in statistical method, correlation search bias, or environmental change I have not measured).

Exact repetitions reflect genuine quasi-periodic recurrence in the measured physical system: pendulum_lab and resonator_obs are sampling from a narrower, more cyclical state space (e.g., thermal oscillation, mechanical resonance, or environmental forcing on 4–8 day timescale) causing identical conditions to recur and produce identical readings.

Exact repetitions result from data-logging or digitization saturation: pendulum_lab and resonator_obs operate at or near their minimum observable resolution (0.0001 units), so when true physical variations fall below this threshold, repeated measurements of nominally different physical states map to identical logged values.

Exact repetitions are an artifact of the correlation/lag-search method: I computed exact repetition statistics by scanning all possible offsets and lags, maximizing the chance of finding long runs by construction. Under the null (white noise), the longest exact run expected is ~1, but the distribution of longest runs has a long tail, and with 4 instruments and multiple lag searches, the probability of observing one or two runs of 12–16 elements is higher than 10^-6.

Pendulum_lab and resonator_obs have undergone a change in measurement protocol, calibration, or firmware between day 10 and day 11 that compressed their output range or introduced a periodic correction, causing false exact matches.

The negative autocorrelations at 4–8 day lags, weak cross-correlations at multi-day offsets, and the pattern of exact repetitions all reflect a genuinely multi-day oscillatory process in the settlement environment (thermal, mechanical, or operational) that is beginning to express itself; post-baseline drifts and repetitions are transient signatures of entry into this oscillatory regime.
